arguments.command:
python3 - <<'PY'
p='/workspace/submission/controller.py';s=open(p).read()
old='''    circulation = _fill_circulation(ctx, best_ratio, circulation)
    simplex = NetworkSimplex(ctx['node_count'], arcs, circulation)
    simplex.solve(special=_make_special(ctx))
    flow_values = list(simplex.flow)

    # Recover the assignment and the exact lexicographic objective values.
'''
new='''    circulation = _fill_circulation(ctx, best_ratio, circulation)

    def solve_and_certify(use_fast_search):
        candidate = NetworkSimplex(ctx['node_count'], arcs, circulation)
        if use_fast_search:
            candidate.solve(special=_make_special(ctx))
        else:
            candidate.solve()
        candidate_potentials = candidate.potentials()
        if len(candidate_potentials) != ctx['node_count']:
            raise RuntimeError('potential count')
        for i, (u, v, lower, upper, cost) in enumerate(arcs):
            amount = candidate.flow[i]
            if not lower <= amount <= upper:
                raise RuntimeError('simplex bound')
            reduced = cost + candidate_potentials[u] - candidate_potentials[v]
            if amount < upper and reduced < 0:
                raise RuntimeError('simplex forward certificate')
            if amount > lower and -reduced < 0:
                raise RuntimeError('simplex backward certificate')
        return candidate

    try:
        simplex = solve_and_certify(True)
    except Exception:
        # The fast range-search pivot rule is only an optimization.  A full
        # scan is slower but uses exactly the same circulation formulation.
        simplex = solve_and_certify(False)
    flow_values = list(simplex.flow)

    # Recover the assignment and the exact lexicographic objective values.
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
